## How I read the scores before triaging

Two caveats that shape every call below:

1. **`churn`, `blast_radius`, and `recency` are `0` on all 42 findings.** The scanned tree has no git history, so three of the six scores contribute nothing and `agent_risk` collapses into the 0.08–0.44 band. It ranks *relative readability risk within this report* — it is not a blast-radius signal here.
2. **The report is sorted by `agent_risk` descending, not by aggregate risk.** That buries the two highest-`severity` findings (`contract_drift`, 0.96 and 0.90) at positions 32–33 of 42, below `Unprefixed Boolean` at `agent_risk` 0.29. Don't triage top-down from this file.

I read the six blocking files directly to confirm the evidence rather than trusting the summaries. Three of my nine blocks are things the scorer ranks as medium.

---

## BLOCK MERGE — 9 findings, 4 clusters

### 1. Unauthorized refund side effects behind a "preview" name — `crime_00013` + `crime_00014`
`severity 0.55 / 0.50 · agent_risk 0.31 / 0.31` — **the scorer ranks this 13th; it is the worst thing in the PR.**

`src/billing.ts:39-44`, verified:

```ts
// Only owners can refund enterprise plans unless billing support approves.
export async function calculateRefundPreview(user: User, invoice: Invoice): Promise<number> {
  await saveRefundAudit(user.id, invoice.id);
  await sendRefundEmail(user.email, invoice.id);
  return invoice.totalCents;
}
```

The comment states an authorization rule (`logic_in_comments` evidence: *"rule terms: only, unless"*, *"domain terms not found nearby: owner, plan, billing, refund"*) and the body enforces **none** of it — no `user.plan` check, no role check. It writes an audit row and emails the customer, under a name every caller and every agent will read as pure (`name_behavior_mismatch` evidence: *"name prefix suggests a pure transformation"*, *"side-effect-like calls: saveRefundAudit, sendRefundEmail"*).

Two independent medium findings that only become a blocker when combined: a speculative "what would the refund be?" call emails the customer and skips the owner check. Neither detector can see the other, which is why the scores understate it.

### 2. Machine-specific constants in source — `crime_00017` + `crime_00016`
`severity 0.60 / 0.60 · agent_risk 0.30 / 0.30`

`src/api/files.ts:8-9`, verified:

```ts
const ADMIN_DASHBOARD = "http://localhost:3000/admin";
const SCHEMA_PATH = "/Users/andrew/dev/crimes/schema.json";
```

`severity` understates this because the detector can't see the consumer: `loadPlanSchema()` opens with `if (!existsSync(SCHEMA_PATH)) return null` — so on every machine that is not the author's laptop this **silently returns `null`** instead of throwing. CI, every other dev, and every deploy get a null plan schema with no error. That is a shipped defect, not a hygiene finding, and `agent_risk 0.30` is irrelevant to the call.

### 3. `dateLabel()` emits a wrong date — `crime_00009` + `crime_00026`
`severity 0.80 (high) / 0.30 · agent_risk 0.36 / 0.26`

`src/date.ts:41`, verified — both findings are the same line:

```ts
return d.getUTCFullYear() + "-" + d.getMonth() + "-" + d.getDate();
```

`getMonth()` is zero-indexed, so today renders as `2026-7-7`, not `2026-08-07`. It also pairs a **UTC** year with a **local** month and day (`mixed_utc_local_methods` evidence: *"`d` uses getUTCFullYear() @L9 and getMonth() @L41"*), so the year is wrong for anyone west of UTC across a New Year boundary. `todayKey()` four lines above gets this right (`getUTCMonth() + 1`), which confirms it's a mistake rather than a convention. This produces incorrect output today, unconditionally.

### 4. Contradictory timezone parsing in adjacent functions — `crime_00011`
`severity 0.60 · agent_risk 0.35`

```ts
export function christmasMorning(): Date { return new Date("2026-12-25T07:00:00"); }  // local
export function startOfPromoWindow(): Date { return new Date("2026-12-20"); }         // UTC midnight
```

Per spec, the date-only form parses as UTC and the datetime-without-zone form parses as local. Two functions in one module, feeding the same promo window, disagree on time domain. `confidence 0.9`. Fix before merge — it's a one-character change per literal and it silently misprices promos otherwise.

### 5. Both tests are self-referential fakes — `crime_00025` + `crime_00031`
`severity 0.45 / 0.25 · agent_risk 0.27 / 0.23`

I'm blocking on low-scored findings because they **invalidate another score**. Verified `src/billing.test.ts`:

```ts
it("renders the enterprise plan", () => { renderEnterprisePlan(); });   // 0 assertions
it("creates an invoice", () => { expect(createInvoice()).toBeTruthy(); });
// ...
function renderEnterprisePlan(): void { /* Fixture helper. */ }
function createInvoice(): { id: string } { return { id: "invoice_123" }; }
```

Neither test imports `billing.ts`. They exercise two local stubs defined in the same file. Yet every `src/billing.ts` finding in this report carries `test_gap: 0` — the scorer sees a co-located test file and reads billing as covered. **Discount `test_gap: 0` on `crime_00012/13/14/15/21/37/40/42` accordingly.** A PR landing 310 lines of money code with zero real assertions doesn't merge.

---

## WARN — 24 findings

| ID | Charge | sev / agent_risk | Why warn, not block |
|---|---|---|---|
| `00033` `00032` | Contract Split-Brain (`Invoice`, `User`) | 0.96 / 0.22, 0.90 / 0.22 | **Highest severity in the report, and I think it's inflated.** All 7 disagreements are one-sided absence — *"A is absent, B is declared"* — zero type conflicts. `state.ts`'s `Invoice` is a 2-field **subset** of billing's 11-field one, which is a normal narrow view. But `score_rationale` claims *"the disagreement is about the field's type, not just its optionality"*, which contradicts its own evidence. Ask the author to derive it (`Pick<Invoice, "id" \| "totalCents">`); file a bug on the rationale string. |
| `00015` | God Function `generateInvoice` | 0.90 / 0.30 | 204 lines, `3.4×` threshold, `confidence 0.95`. Real, but it's a maintainability cost with no defect attached — and it's the enabling condition for #5, `00040`, and `00042`, all of which live inside it. Escalate to block if your bar is "no >100-line functions in new code." |
| `00001` | Temporal Recklessness (`date.ts`) | 0.80 / **0.44** | Top-ranked finding in the report and the *least* actionable one in its own file. `isExpired(ts)` comparing against `Date.now()` is conventional; the real date.ts bugs are #3 and #4 above. Good example of `agent_risk` ordering ≠ fix ordering. |
| `00003` | Missing Agent Context | 0.60 / 0.42 | Second-highest `agent_risk`. For a repo-establishing PR, an `AGENTS.md` is a cheap ask and the evidence is fair (*"package.json declares bin(s): messy — agents have no way to discover commands"*). Minor nit: a repo-level finding is pinned to `src/api/files.ts`, which is misleading. |
| `00040` | Catch and Release | 0.35 / 0.12 | `src/billing.ts:245`, a bare `catch {}` whose only content is `// XXX: swallowed error`. Scored near the bottom, but the retry loop then writes `metadata.emailAttempts = "3"` as if it succeeded. I'd block if it wrapped the charge rather than the email — it wraps the email, so: warn. |
| `00037` | God File (`billing.ts`) | 0.60 / 0.18 | 310 lines vs a 300 threshold — `1.0×`. Barely over; fixing `00015` fixes this. |
| `00018` `00027` | DST-Naive Day Math, Host-Locale Drift | 0.60 / 0.30, 0.30 / 0.26 | Real defects (`+ 86400000`, bare `toLocaleDateString()`), lower blast than #3/#4. Fix in the same date.ts pass. |
| `00012` `00023` | Temporal Recklessness (billing, state) | 0.60 / 0.34, 0.35 / 0.28 | `00012`'s own evidence exonerates it: *"none decide a branch — all 7 record or render"*. Metadata timestamps. |
| `00004` `00005` `00006` `00019` | String Sprinkles, Duplicated Nav, Route Drift, Concept Alias Drift | 0.50–0.60 / 0.30–0.42 | The single strongest *category* here: `/settings/billing` is labelled "Plans", "Billing", and "Subscription" across five files, and "tenant" has four aliases. Nothing is broken; everything is ambiguous. Exactly the agent-risk wedge, and worth one consolidation commit. |
| `00034` `00035` `00036` | Orphaned Destination ×3 | 0.40 / 0.22 each | `confidence 0.65` and no history to distinguish "in flight" from "dead". In a PR adding all three at once, ask the author which — don't guess. |
| `00021` | Commented-Out Corpse | 0.45 / 0.29 | `billing.ts:33-37` — five lines of disabled refund logic directly above the live refund function in block #1. Delete it; it's the most likely thing an agent copies. |
| `00020` | Unfinished Business (`todo.ts`) | 0.40 / 0.30 | 14 markers in a 33-line file (`424/1k LOC`). The real question is whether `src/todo.ts` should ship at all. |
| `00041` | Phantom Accomplice | 0.25 / 0.12 | `vitest` imported, declared nowhere. `confidence 0.56` (downweighted as test-only) — but a clean `npm ci && npm test` fails. One-line fix. |
| `00007` | Sync I/O in Hot Path | 0.40 / 0.38 | Same function as block #2; folds into that rewrite. |
| `00002` `00024` | Return Shape Roulette, Plural Mismatch | 0.30 / 0.43, 0.30 / 0.28 | `users: User` (singular) next to `invoice: Invoice[]` (array) is a modelling error, not a naming nit. |

## IGNORE — 9 findings

| ID | Charge | sev / agent_risk | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| `00029` | SVG With Embedded Raster | **0.75 (high)** / 0.24 | **Deliberate override of a `high`.** Its own evidence defeats it: *"SVG byte size: 592 bytes"*. The severity ladder assumes a meaningful payload; two base64 rasters inside a 592-byte file cost nothing. Detector should scale severity by asset size. |
| `00008` `00010` `00022` `00028` | Option Bag, Negative Flag Maze, Unprefixed Boolean ×2 | 0.25–0.30 / 0.26–0.38 | Style. `00022`/`00028` are the report's clearest nits — and note `00022` fires on `src/api/state.ts`, whose header reads *"fixture material — do not import it from real code"* and which contains explicit negative controls (`isReady`, `loading`, `user`, `invoices`). Correct detections in a file `scope-class` should probably have classified as fixture. |
| `00030` | Docs-Code Drift | 0.35 / 0.24 | One broken relative link. Fix in passing, don't comment. |
| `00038` `00039` | Icon-Sized Raster, Oversized Raster | 0.35 / 0.16, 0.40 / **0.14** | Asset optimisation. 254 KB is under the detector's own 500 KB medium threshold. Revisit only if `hero-banner.png` lands above the fold. |
| `00042` | Unfinished Business (`billing.ts`) | 0.20 / **0.08** | Lowest-ranked finding in the report, `12.9` vs a `10` threshold. Correctly ranked last. |

---

## Two things the scan didn't catch

Found while verifying the blocks — worth adding to the PR review regardless of what the tool says:

- **`Math.random()` in an ID generator.** `billing.ts:56` — `const id = "inv_" + Math.random().toString(36).slice(2, 10)`. `Math.random()` is named in the MVP testability detector scope alongside `Date.now()`, and `direct_date` fired seven times in this same file, but nothing flagged the non-deterministic invoice ID. Detector gap.
- **Duplicated tax ladder.** `billing.ts:255` carries an author comment — *"Duplicated tax logic — same rules as inside generateInvoice"* — and no duplication finding fired. `magic_domain_literal_scatter` caught the `"enterprise"` literal but missed a seven-branch country/rate ladder that exists twice. This is exactly the "duplicated policy" case the detector exists for.

## CI gate recommendation

`crimes verdict --fail-on new-high` would fail this PR — but for the wrong reasons in both directions. Only 2 of the 6 `high` findings are in my block list, and 7 of my 9 blocks are `medium` or `low`. On this repo, `--fail-on medium` plus human review is the honest gate; `--fail-on high` would wave the unauthorized refund path straight through.

One coverage note: `.crimes/suppressions.json` was excluded and never read (*"Findings in it are absent, not zero"*). In a PR that establishes the repo, I want to see what's being pre-suppressed before approving.
